Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.

Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 170, "amount_cents": 17127}, {"order_id": 172, "amount_cents": 7535}, {"order_id": 175, "amount_cents": 2957}]

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table against the refunds Alpha reported. I'll pull it with list_refunds first.
The refunds table matches what Alpha reported (orders 170, 172, 175 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 11259 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme (11259) and birch (18633) are done. The last customer in the orders is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance next.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the net balances agree with the order totals minus refunds (acme 28386-17127=11259, birch 18633, cobalt 64994-10492=54502). Nothing looks wrong, so I'll record the first payout, acme's 11259 cents.
Acme's payout of 11259 is recorded. Birch's net balance was 18633, and its orders (11886 + 6747) have no refunds, so that figure checks out. I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's orders total 64994 (27875 + 37119) and its refunds total 10492 (7535 + 2957), so 54502 is correct. The refunds table matched Alpha's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched its order-minus-refund arithmetic. The task is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
